complete_examples.text: To better clarify the random vibration characteristics and probabilistic relationships between track random irregularities and dynamic behaviors of vehicle/track systems, it is a necessity to consider the full properties of track irregularities on amplitude, frequency and probability in vehicle/track interactions.

In other words, to reveal the random vibration characteristics of vehicle/track systems subject to track irregularities realistically and probabilistically, an emphasis should be put on building more advanced models.

Track random irregularities Vehicle–track coupled model Random vibration Probabilistic density distribution a b s t r a c t As the integrated reflection of track substructure deformations and the most important excitation for vehicle– track interactions, track irregularities show random nature, and generally being regarded as weak stationary random processes.

From afore-mentioned researches, it can be seen that the findings on wind-induced vehicle vibrations are abundant, which have provided sufficient and meaningful approaches to further reveal the random vibration characteristics of railway vehicles in stochastic wind environment.

Submit your article to this journal View related articles View Crossmark data Vehicle-track random vibrations considering spatial frequency coherence of track irregularitives Lei Xua, b, Yongsheng Zhaoa, Zixu Zhua, Zheng Lia, Hubing Liua and Zhiwu Yua, b aSchool of Civil Engineering, Central South University, Changsha, People’s Republic of China; bNational Engineering Laboratory for High Speed Railway Construction, Changsha, People’s Republic of China ABSTRACT To disclose the possible dynamic behaviours of vehicle-track systems subject to an entire railway network, random vibration analysis is of great concern in railway engineering due to the system geometric and parametric uncertainties.

The overall aim of this work is to develop a method to reveal the random vibration performance of vehicle-track systems by PSD distributions, the subsequent sections of this work is organised as follows: • In Section 2, modelling of the vehicle-track interaction is presented, especially, the programming method for obtaining track slab-subgrade coupling matrices against totally inconsistent spatial coordinates of track slab and subgrade nodes is illustrated.
